title: The fourth dimension: physiological resilience as an independent determinant of endurance exercise performance
population: Endurance athletes (review of laboratory and field evidence)
findings: VO2max, economy and fractional utilisation are not static: they are prone to significant deterioration as fatiguing endurance exercise proceeds.
Critical power may fall by an average of 10% following 2 h of heavy-intensity cycling.
Individual changes in CP ranged from under 1% to about 32%, so inter-individual variability is appreciable.
The mechanistic basis for differences in fatigue resistance is not resolved.
Argues physiological resilience should be an additional (fourth) component in models of endurance performance.
limitations: Narrative perspective; the quantitative example in the abstract is from cycling and mechanisms are unresolved. Crossref gives online date 2023-08-22; print issue is J Physiol 2024 Sep;602(17):4113-4128, and the 2024 print year is recorded.
implications: Default prior for fatigued threshold or critical-speed decline after about 2 h of heavy-intensity work: about 10% (range under 1% to about 32%), to be personalised from the athlete's own data. This is a cycling-derived prior; treat it as unvalidated for running.
Add a resilience term to the performance and pacing model for marathon and longer plans instead of using only start-line CS or LT.

verification.notes: Crossref title, journal, first author match; online 2023, print 2024. All numbers (10%, <1% to ~32%, 2 h heavy cycling) present in PubMed abstract.
